summary_html: Agency **files a court petition** to open a **dependency** (or similar) case. Federal funding frameworks (IV-E/ASFA) link court oversight, reasonable-efforts findings, and permanency timelines to downstream actions.
authority_html:
- **ASFA / SSA Title IV-E** — court findings; timelines; permanency planning  
- **CFSR (45 CFR Part 1355)** — federal review of court/agency performance measures

case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.holding: A CHINS adjudication was affirmed because the merits inquiry is directed at the child's welfare rather than each parent's individual fitness, which is addressed at disposition, and the State's burden is a preponderance of the evidence.
key_cases.relevance: B.R. is the controlling statement of what the State must prove when it files a CHINS petition, and of the child-centered focus of the merits stage.
key_cases.quote: The focus of the CHINS proceeding was on B.R.'s welfare; the question of father's fitness to parent B.R. will be addressed at disposition.

key_cases.holding: The Court remanded for ICWA notice to the Mohawk Tribe because the trial court had reason to believe an Indian child was involved, and otherwise affirmed the CHINS merits and disposition orders, holding the preponderance standard governs a CHINS adjudication and that merits and disposition orders must rest on findings of fact.
key_cases.relevance: It fixes the burden the State carries once a CHINS petition is filed and opens the dependency case.
key_cases.quote: the standard of proof for a CHINS adjudication is that the findings be supported by a preponderance of the evidence

key_cases.case_name: In re A.O. & I.O., Juveniles & In re B.G. & E.G., Juveniles
key_cases.holding: The CHINS merits and disposition orders for four children were reversed and vacated as unsupported by the findings or the record, and the orders allowing a party's advocate to inspect the other children's juvenile records without a need-to-know designation were reversed.
key_cases.relevance: The case shows that a CHINS petition must be proved as to the circumstances existing when it was filed, and that domestic violence by one adult plus later non-engagement with DCF is not automatically enough.
key_cases.quote: We therefore reverse the CHINS merits determination as unsupported by the findings or the record.

key_cases.holding: The CHINS determination was reversed because the evidence did not support the ground the State pleaded, and the Court declined to reach the disposition order transferring custody to DCF.
key_cases.relevance: The State must prove the specific CHINS ground alleged in its petition and cannot have the adjudication upheld on an alternative theory.
key_cases.quote: For these reasons, we reverse the family division's determination that J.N. was CHINS.

key_cases.case_name: W.H. v. Department for Children and Families
key_cases.holding: Refusal to register an Alabama order awarding the father sole custody was affirmed because Vermont had already commenced and was exercising jurisdiction over the juvenile in conformity with the UCCJEA as her home state, so Alabama could not simultaneously exercise jurisdiction and neither the UCCJEA nor the PKPA obliged Vermont to recognize its order.
key_cases.relevance: W.H. is Vermont's authority on which state may open and keep a dependency case when an out-of-state parent holds or seeks a competing custody order, and it confirms that CHINS, neglect and termination proceedings are 'child custody proceedings' under the UCCJEA.
key_cases.quote: The simultaneous-jurisdiction provision of the UCCJEA precludes a court from exercising jurisdiction if a proceeding "has been commenced in a court of another state having jurisdiction" under the UCCJEA.

timeline_requirements.deadline: 24 hours to document the safety determination and safety plan on the SDM Safety Assessment
timeline_requirements.starts_from: First in-person interview with the family
timeline_requirements.consequence_of_miss: Not specified in Vermont DCF Family Services Policy 52 (effective 9/5/2024).

timeline_requirements.deadline: 60 days to conclude an investigation; 45 days to complete an assessment, or 60 days with written justification and supervisor approval
timeline_requirements.starts_from: Opening of the child safety intervention (the investigation or assessment track)
timeline_requirements.consequence_of_miss: Not specified in Vermont DCF Family Services Policy 52 (effective 9/5/2024); the policy allows an investigation to stay open past 60 days while a law enforcement or criminal case is unresolved, and an assessment extension may not exceed 60 days total (33 V.S.A. § 4915a(b)). Vermont sets no completion deadline for the investigation track by statute (33 V.S.A. § 4915b).
